card.title: Presentation and debate — structure spoken aloud

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Spoken English is writing with breath: presentations run hook → signposted points → verdict (with visual aids supporting, never reading); debates run motion → definition → arguments → rebuttal → summing (points of information welcomed, heckling never); discussions trade turns with discourse markers (building on that…, to counter…); listening comprehension hunts gist, detail and inference across one hearing. Role plays rehearse real situations — interviews, complaints, requests — with register matched to role.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: presentation: hook + map + 3 points + verdict (+ Q&A)  ·  debate speech: definition + 2–3 arguments (claim+evidence) + rebuttal + summary  ·  discussion moves: agree/build/qualify/challenge + reason  ·  listening: predict → listen → verify (gist first, detail second)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Debates need the motion DEFINED before arguing (this house = scope lock). Presentations need timing rehearsal (10 slides ≈ 10 minutes breaks without practice). Role plays need briefs (who wants what); listening answers need the exact asked form (word limit, true/false/not-given discipline).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Points of information: accept, answer briefly, resume — refusing everything looks weak. Nerves management: breath, notes-as-map (never script), eye contact in thirds. Listening traps: distractors echoing question words with wrong details; order rarely matches option order.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Two-minute motion speech drill ('Phones belong in classrooms'): define (regulated classroom use) → argument 1 (research tool + evidence) → argument 2 (emergency contact) → rebuttal (distraction solved by pouches/policy) → summary (tool, not toy). Five beats, timed, rebuttal mandatory.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Rhetoric persuades beyond evidence — debate rewards the better speaker, not the truer cause (judges must separate). Scripted 'role plays' test memory, not interaction; markers reward spontaneous repair. One hearing caps listening fairness — accents and speed vary uncontrollably.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From the written essay outward: thesis becomes stance, paragraphs become timed points, transitions become signposts ('my second argument…'), conclusion becomes verdict-plus-appeal. Listening derives from prediction: pre-read questions to build an information grid, then listen INTO the grid slots.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Speak in triplets (three points, three examples). Signpost everything ('first… second… finally'). Debate: define + rebut + summarise — the three non-negotiables. Listening: underline question keywords first, then listen for synonyms, not echoes.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: debate-speech outline on a motion; presentation plan with visual-aid notes; role-play dialogue in register; listening tasks (gist + detail + inference) from one hearing.
